mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4% in the month preceding the forecast period coincides with a decline in near-term expected corporate credit spreads, reducing financing costs and thereby driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the preceding month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero under the same trigger (t-test p > 0.05) or credit spread widening offsets the rate hike effect.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in unemployment claims below the prior month's level (after a downward trend) indicates a cooling labor market, prompting market participants to anticipate a weaker consumer demand cycle and thus negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS shows two consecutive monthly declines followed by a single monthly increase below the prior low
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05) during similar labor market transitions.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the monthly Housing Starts index (above prior month's high by at least 10%) signals renewed builder confidence and accelerating domestic demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly value exceeds prior month's high by ≥10%
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative or flat despite the signal, or Housing Starts fails to sustain momentum over the next two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in Industrial Production by at least 2% for three consecutive months suggests weakening supply-side capacity, which raises the cost of capital and reduces corporate earnings expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant during analogous contractionary supply shocks.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals sticky inflation expectations that prompt the Fed to maintain higher policy rates, which compresses equity discount rates and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant during similar inflation spikes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% for two consecutive months in the absence of wage growth signals a tight labor market, prompting equity market pricing of higher future inflation and slower growth, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.0% for two consecutive months without a parallel rise in average hourly earnings
regime_hint: Labor market tightening without wage acceleration
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant during comparable labor market conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden, one-time drop in retail sales (as proxied by PAYEMS) of at least 3% month-over-month followed by two consecutive months of flat or rising sales indicates a demand shock, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly value falls by ≥3% in a single month followed by two months of ≥0% change
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during analogous demand shocks.

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of industrial production to capacity utilization (implied by INDPRO and HOUST) falls below 0.7 for three consecutive months, it signals underutilized capacity and potential for future supply-side easing, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO/HOUST ratio < 0.7 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain flat or negative despite the signal, or the ratio fails to re-enter the normal range within 6 months.
